references.text: The ash from the sin offering was to be brought outside the camp to a clean place, just as here in Leviticus.
The ash from the red heifer was to be gathered and placed on a clean spot outside the camp, corresponding to the instruction about where the ash should be kept.
The priest's garments were holy and were to be used in service; changing clothes for different tasks highlights the importance of holiness.
Ezekiel describes that priests must take off their holy garments before going out to the people, so as not to make the people holy with their clothing.
The remainder of the bull from the sin offering was to be brought outside the camp to a clean place where the ash was emptied out.
On the Day of Atonement, the remains of the sin offering were to be burned outside the camp, and whoever burned it had to wash his clothes.
The book of Hebrews explains that Jesus suffered outside the city gate in order to make the people holy, a typological parallel to how the ash was carried outside the camp.
